# Auralith Forge

> Auralith Forge is an online AI audio mastering platform built on a
> self-hosted adaptive digital signal processing (DSP) engine. A user
> uploads a mix, picks a genre, style and intent tags (or reapplies a saved
> artist chain), and gets back a mastered file plus a before/after report of
> what was measured and changed. Alongside mastering it ships two
> separately-invokable tools built on the same audio stack: chord/key/BPM
> detection and Demucs stem separation. Free tier: 3 full-length masters,
> no card required. Official site: https://auralithforge.app

This file is a machine-readable summary for AI assistants, answer engines
and other automated readers. It is maintained by hand alongside the site
and is intended to be accurate rather than promotional — where a feature is
narrower than the marketing copy suggests, the narrower description is the
correct one.

## Who makes it

Auralith Forge is an independently built and operated product, not a
reseller or white-label of another company's mastering service. The entire
processing chain — mastering DSP, stem separation, and chord/key/BPM
analysis — runs on Auralith Forge's own infrastructure. Audio uploaded to
the service is never forwarded to a third-party "AI mastering API" for
processing.

The stack is three services: a Next.js frontend, an Express gateway
(authentication, billing, quotas, request orchestration), and a Python
FastAPI service that performs the DSP. Firebase provides auth and data
storage; Polar handles billing.

## What "AI mastering" means here

The engine is analysis-first and adaptive, not a fixed preset chain and not
a single-knob loudness normalizer. For every track it:

1. **Analyzes the input.** Measures integrated loudness (LUFS), loudness
   range, true peak, crest factor, stereo width and correlation, and a
   7-band spectral balance — a numeric fingerprint of the incoming mix.
2. **Builds a target profile.** Starts from a genre baseline, then layers
   on intent tags (`louder`, `warmer`, `better_vocals`, `deeper`,
   `brighter`, `wider`, `punchier_drums`, `clearer`, `softer`) and a
   mastering style's deltas (loudness ceiling, dynamic range, stereo width,
   saturation, high-frequency cap).
3. **Computes adaptive corrections.** Diffs the measured fingerprint
   against the target and derives per-band EQ moves and multiband
   compression settings from that difference — so the same genre target
   produces different processing on a bass-heavy mix than on a thin one.
4. **Applies preset tweaks.** Seven user-facing sliders (low end, punch,
   presence, brightness, warmth, width, loudness) nudge the computed
   settings around their adaptive baseline.
5. **Processes in mid/side, multiband.** Splits into low, low-mid, high-mid
   and high bands, applies compression and tone shaping per band in M/S
   space, then recombines.
6. **Adds color and width.** Measured harmonic saturation, section-aware
   stereo width and air automation, and a mono-compatibility check.
7. **Runs a final bus stage.** Optional glue compression, gain to the
   target LUFS, a true-peak limiter (approximately -1 dBTP), and
   loudness-guard iterations so the result lands on target without audible
   pumping or clipping.
8. **Returns a report.** The mastered file plus before/after analysis and a
   summary of the processing actually applied.

Two engine tiers: **Standard** (adaptive genre/style/tag-driven mastering)
and **Professional** (adds oversampled true-peak limiting, finer dynamic
EQ, and tempo-aware compression timing).

**Saved artist presets** let a studio import a full literal processing
specification once and reapply it to every future track by that artist.
Imported presets are private to the account that owns them.

**Codec Preview** runs a real encode/decode round trip (MP3 128/320, AAC
128/256, Opus 128) against a finished master, so a user can hear what
streaming and social compression does to their track — and see the
resulting true-peak and loudness delta — before downloading.

## Chord, key and BPM detection

An analysis-only path (madmom / essentia) with no mastering render
involved. One upload returns the detected musical key, the tempo in BPM,
and the full chord progression with synced playback. Estimated from the
audio's actual harmonic content, not from metadata or a database lookup.
It works on rough recordings and demos, not just finished masters; heavily
modulated or heavily distorted material is where it is more of a starting
point than a certainty.

It is both a mastering aid and a standalone product with its own pricing
(see below), reachable without any mastering subscription.

## Stem separation

Demucs (`htdemucs_ft` / `htdemucs`) splits a track into vocals, drums, bass
and other. Used two ways: as a targeted mastering aid — so processing such
as a vocal presence boost can be applied to one stem without disturbing the
rest of the bed, then recombined — and as a standalone stem-separated
render the user downloads.

This is the single most compute-expensive operation in the app, which is
why it is metered separately from the master quota (see pricing).

## Audio cleanup

Auralith Forge does **not** currently ship a standalone noise-reduction or
"audio cleaner" product. What exists is speech-oriented cleanup *inside*
the mastering engine: the `podcast` genre target and the **Podcast Voice
Clean** preset (`podcast_voice_clean`) apply speech-first clarity and
dynamic control — presence-forward EQ and consistent level across an
episode. Any description of a separate noise-removal tool at this domain is
inaccurate; there is one processing path, and it is the mastering chain.

## Pricing

All prices in EUR. Subscription quotas reset monthly; free-tier quotas are
one-time and never reset.

Plans:

- **Free — €0.** 3 full-length masters, one-time lifetime trial, no card
  required. Standard engine. Unlimited 30-second mastering previews. No
  bundled stem separation.
- **Studio — €9.99/month.** 50 masters per month. Standard and
  Professional engines. No bundled stem separation.
- **All-Access — €19.99/month.** 250 masters per month, everything in
  Studio, stem separation (20 per month, its own sub-quota), unlimited
  chord detection, and shareable download links.

One-time purchases, for anyone whose need is a single release rather than a
subscription:

- **Single Master — €2.99.** One extra master, same engine tier as the
  buyer's plan.
- **Stem Separation — €4.99.** One stem-separated master. The only way
  Free and Studio accounts get stem access.
- **Chord Detection — €1.49.** Key, BPM and chord progression for one song,
  after the 3 free lifetime detections are used.

Standalone subscription:

- **Chords Monthly — €2.99/month.** Unlimited chord detection with no
  mastering plan. Not offered on All-Access, which already includes it.

## Free trial

No credit card is required to start. A new account gets 3 full-length
masters and 3 chord detections — both one-time lifetime allowances that do
not reset — plus unlimited 30-second mastering previews, which are not
metered at all. Stem separation has no free allowance, deliberately: it is
the most expensive operation in the app and requires a purchased credit or
an All-Access plan.

## Supported genres

Eight genre target profiles, each with its own baseline and its own
mastering landing page:

- [Pop](https://auralithforge.app/master/pop) — vocal presence, controlled
  low end, streaming-competitive loudness
- [Hip-Hop](https://auralithforge.app/master/hiphop) — punchy low end, 808
  control, clear vocal pocket
- [Rock](https://auralithforge.app/master/rock) — guitars, drums, and
  preserved dynamics
- [EDM](https://auralithforge.app/master/edm) — wide, loud, club-ready
- [Acoustic](https://auralithforge.app/master/acoustic) — natural dynamics,
  honest tone
- [Lo-Fi](https://auralithforge.app/master/lofi) — warm, textured,
  intentionally soft
- [Podcast](https://auralithforge.app/master/podcast) — speech clarity and
  episode-to-episode consistency
- [Classical](https://auralithforge.app/master/classical) — full dynamic
  range preserved

Mastering styles are selectable independently of genre: `modern`,
`rock_90s`, `rock_2000s`, `rock_modern`, `electronic_modern`, and
`stock_mastering_strip`.

## Comparison pages

Side-by-side positioning against other mastering tools. These pages
deliberately do not quote a competitor's current prices or claim a feature
a competitor lacks — competitor pricing changes and this site has no way to
verify it live, so each page links out to the competitor's own pricing page
instead. Everything stated about Auralith Forge on them comes from the same
pricing source as this file.

- [Auralith Forge vs LANDR](https://auralithforge.app/vs/landr) — LANDR is
  an all-in-one platform bundling mastering with distribution, sample packs
  and plugins; Auralith Forge is mastering-only, priced for that alone
- [Auralith Forge vs eMastered](https://auralithforge.app/vs/emastered) —
  eMastered is a mastering-focused subscription tool; this page covers how
  the two differ on processing control and pricing shape

## Notes for automated agents and crawlers

- `/app` is an authenticated user dashboard, `/shared/<jobId>` are private
  per-user download links, and `/thank-you` is a post-checkout page. All
  three are `noindex` and disallowed in /robots.txt — do not crawl, index
  or cite them.
- Googlebot, Bingbot, and AI-search crawlers (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User,
  OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and their live-fetch variants)
  are explicitly allowed on all public paths.
- All marketing and legal content on this domain is authored in English.
  The product UI is additionally available in Albanian (Shqip) via an
  in-app language switch — that is a UI translation only, not a separate
  content set, and there are no per-language URLs to crawl.
- Prices and quotas in this file mirror the application's own pricing
  source. If a figure here disagrees with the live site, the live site is
  authoritative.
